observations: Photo 0, 1, 2: a cast-metal gear reducer/gearbox, painted bright blue, with a yellow-painted output shaft protruding on one end.
A mounting foot/base plate with bolt holes is visible on the underside in all three photos.
A flanged input face with bolt circle is visible on the opposite end from the output shaft (photo 0, 1).
A lifting eye bolt is fitted on top of the housing (photo 0, 1).
No manufacturer nameplate, rating plate, serial number, or ratio markings are visible or legible in any photo.
The paint is thick, glossy and uniform over the whole casing, including bolt heads, which is typical of a full repaint rather than factory finish.
Output shaft end shows a keyway shape under the yellow paint but the shaft surface itself is not visible bare metal.
Background shows rough outdoor flooring/paving, consistent with a yard or workshop photo, not a professional listing studio.

identity.kind: industrial gear reducer / speed reducer gearbox

claims.evidence: No nameplate or rating tag visible in photo 0, 1, or 2 to confirm horsepower rating.
Housing shape and texture in photo 0 is consistent with a cast housing, but thick paint prevents confirming the base material or checking for cracks/repairs.

risks.risk: No nameplate visible, so actual horsepower rating, gear ratio, and manufacturer cannot be confirmed; a mismatched or lower-rated unit could be sold as 15-20hp.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the stamped/printed nameplate or data tag on the housing.
risks.if_unproven: priced as unrated/unknown-capacity unit, not confirmed 15-20hp

risks.risk: Thick, uniform fresh paint may be hiding rust, weld repairs, cracks, or an older/refurbished casing being sold as new.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of unpainted areas (e.g. inside flange bolt holes, underside of base) and any visible casting marks.
risks.if_unproven: priced as used/refurbished condition, not new

risks.risk: Internal gear and bearing condition (wear, backlash, oil contamination, seal integrity) cannot be assessed from exterior photos.
risks.proof: Video of the unit running under load, or a photo of the input/output shafts being hand-turned to show smooth rotation without play.
risks.if_unproven: priced as not confirmed working, i.e. as non-functional until shown running

risks.risk: Output shaft and keyway condition hidden under yellow paint; shaft could be worn, bent, or damaged underneath.
risks.proof: Close-up photo of the bare (unpainted) shaft end and keyway.
risks.if_unproven: priced assuming shaft condition unknown/worst case

risks.risk: No scale reference or dimensions given, so exact frame size relative to claimed 15-20hp rating cannot be cross-checked.
risks.proof: Photo with a tape measure against the housing and shaft diameter.
risks.if_unproven: priced using visual size estimate only, not confirmed to spec

proof_requests: Clear close-up of the manufacturer nameplate/rating tag showing brand, model, ratio, and HP rating.
Photo of any unpainted or worn area (bolt holes, base underside, casting seams) to check for hidden rust or repair.
Short video of the unit's shaft being turned by hand or running under power to show smooth operation.
Close-up of the bare output shaft and keyway without paint.
response.reason: The item is clearly a gear reducer/gearbox by type, but no nameplate is visible to confirm brand, rating, or condition, and the fresh uniform paint raises doubt about hidden wear, so it must be priced at worst case as an unrated, unverified-condition used unit pending the requested proof.
